claim: People pick between strategies in proportion to learned success rates (close to probability matching), and simple reinforcement or Bayesian success-estimate models fit the choices.
agent_test: Keep per-strategy success counts in memory per task type; choose by noisy success estimate versus fixed or uniform choice, equal tokens.

claim: Adaptivity to a shift in which strategy works depends on noticing the shift, not on working-memory capacity. LLM agents show the same weakness: they keep calling a tool group after its reliability silently changes (d05).
agent_test: Shift strategy success rates mid-session; compare an agent with an explicit 'did the success rate change' check against none.

claim: A person has a repertoire of many strategies and uses different ones on similar problems; strong solvers tailor strategy to problem type.
agent_test: Give the agent a named repertoire of 5-7 strategies and measure whether per-item choice beats the single best fixed strategy.

claim: Recently used strategies are chosen again (priming); the effect is small (.45 vs .41) and tied to context (pure versus mixed blocks).
agent_test: Check whether an agent repeats its last strategy after a failure; compare forced rotation after a fail with free choice.

claim: Weaker solvers keep their own strategy even when shown a better one (kept on 57% of trials) and rarely switch to correct alternatives.
agent_test: Show the agent its own plan next to an alternative plan and measure whether it switches when the alternative is verifiably better.

claim: Analogy transfer depends on noticing: without a hint few solvers apply a stored analog, with a hint most do. Comparing two analogs and nearer sources help.
agent_test: Retrieval-with-cue ablation: the agent writes its own list of similar past problems before solving versus no cue; equal tokens.

claim: Which solution strategy transfers from a source story is contested: a conceptual replication with pupils found no clear effect of source strategy on target strategy (V=.13, p=.105), and control baselines differ (51% vs about 10%).
agent_test: Give the agent an analog with a wrong-strategy solution and see whether it copies the strategy.

claim: Self-generated analog recall as a prompt gives a small gain (GSM8K 75.0 zero-shot to 77.8; MATH 33.0 to 37.3, GPT-3.5); against 5-shot CoT the gain is +1.1 and +2.4.
agent_test: Run analogical recall on our tasks at equal tokens versus plain CoT.

claim: No single prompting strategy wins across datasets or problem sizes; per-item oracles are far above the best fixed strategy.
agent_test: Compute an oracle over our strategy set on a held-out item set to bound the value of any router before building one.

claim: Letting the model choose its own strategy, or merging strategy outputs by vote or verifier, recovers only a fraction of the oracle gap (Phi-4 TruthQuest best single 49.0, vote+prob 57.3, oracle 82.9; ZebraLogic gain under 1 point).
agent_test: Compare self-chosen strategy, majority vote across strategies and a verifier pick at equal tokens.

claim: Cheap-first with escalation on low answer consistency, or learned routing of model and strategy, cuts tokens or cost at equal accuracy (46-85% cost cut in Adaptive-Solver; over 60% fewer tokens in a router).
agent_test: Escalate only when 3-sample agreement is below a threshold; compare tokens and accuracy with always-deep.

claim: Thinking-heavy modes waste tokens on easy items (o1-like models used 1,953% more tokens on 2+3; thinking models gain little on easy tasks) and cut effort near collapse.
agent_test: Measure accuracy per token by item difficulty and test an easy-item shortcut.

claim: Chain-of-thought is not a safe default: tasks where deliberate verbal thinking hurts people also hurt models (artificial grammar: CoT 87.5 to 64.4 for GPT-4o).
agent_test: Include implicit-pattern tasks in our eval and test an 'answer directly' option.

claim: Self-composed task-level reasoning structures help on BBH and T4D (PaLM 2-L 56 to 67; 30 to 69) but a rival study finds free-text per-instance plans beat JSON structures on MATH (75.5 vs 63.5), so the benefit depends on task and format.
agent_test: Task-level plan vs per-instance free-text plan at equal tokens on our mix of tasks.

claim: Having the right strategy does not guarantee success: execution errors dominate (74.7% of Self-Discover MATH failures; giving the full Tower of Hanoi algorithm did not move the collapse point; the right strategy label does not ensure MicroDYN success). Plan-and-Solve error analysis on zero-shot CoT found misunderstanding the largest class (27% vs calculation 7%), so the error mix depends on method.
agent_test: Add step-level checking to plan execution and compare error rate against plan-only.

claim: Abstraction (step-back) helps knowledge-heavy tasks (MMLU Physics 66.4 to 73.2, TimeQA 41.5 to 66) but gives no gain over CoT on GSM8K (84.4 vs 84.3); it fixes 20.5% of baseline errors and adds 11.9% new ones.
agent_test: Apply step-back only to knowledge-heavy items; check net fix and break rates.

claim: Decomposition (least-to-most) gives large gains on length generalization (SCAN at least 99% vs 16%) but small ones on GSM8K (60.97 to 62.39).
agent_test: Use decomposition conditionally on length or compositional depth.

claim: Search over decomposed steps with evaluation (trial and error) beats single-path on Game of 24 (ToT b=5 74% vs CoT 4%); the bottleneck is idea generation, not evaluation. Evidence is mostly one task shape and costs more tokens.
agent_test: Test branching on tasks with early dead ends; track tokens.

claim: A controller that reads a short progress report and picks the next strategy (continue, restart, backtrack, decompose) beats fixed strategy arms (Game of 24: 89 vs ToT 65); removing the bandit drops TheoremQA from 84.13 to 39.46.
agent_test: Add a one-line progress report after each phase and a strategy decision rule; ablate.

claim: Training a small model to choose among CoT, least-to-most and program-of-thought at the first attempt lifts GSM8K by 4-15 points.
agent_test: Not directly testable without training; use as an upper-bound reference for a prompted selector.

claim: In MicroDYN-type tasks, effective exploration (VOTAT) predicts performance but is neither necessary nor sufficient; guessing is common and strategy effects are confounded with reasoning ability.
agent_test: Track whether the agent varies one factor at a time in exploration tasks; compare with success.

claim: Structure knowledge and control performance dissociate (r about .35-.41): some solvers control well with poor knowledge.
agent_test: Probe the agent's stated causal model separately from its action success.

claim: Complex problem solving correlates substantially with intelligence (mean g=.433; 47 studies, N=13,740), but a critique reports near-vanishing correlations among different complex problems after control and incremental validity is about 5% of grade variance; CPS as one general ability is contested.
agent_test: No direct agent test; use as a caution when treating a CPS benchmark as one skill.

claim: Practice on MicroDYN transfers to a real-time task (d=0.40, about 40% transfer), not the reverse, and VOTAT use does not mediate the transfer.
agent_test: Check whether experience with one exploration task helps another in the same agent session.

claim: Under complexity people show an 'emergency reaction' (less self-reflection, stereotyped, hasty action) and good Lohhausen managers switch between analytic and intuitive modes; evidence is qualitative.
schema_part: G (monitoring for hasty or stereotyped action)
agent_test: Log repeated identical actions and unreflected steps in long tasks; trigger a reflection step.

claim: LLMs fail when red herrings are present: GPT-4 solved 6 of 494 walls in the original set but 471 once red herrings were removed; LLM functional-fixedness gaps exist (MacGyver: GPT-4 73.3% vs majority-of-people 79.3%). Counter-evidence: strong reasoning models reached human level on a fixation benchmark (mARC 0.751 vs physicians 0.66), and the one classic-style test (6 items per cell) shows prompt-forced steps, not clear rigidity.
agent_test: Run an Einstellung check: after a failed approach, force a different frame and compare.

claim: LLM agents explore hidden-rule tasks poorly (prefer OR over AND rules); sampling many distinct hypotheses and choosing actions that eliminate them removes the gap, while a typed scaffold alone can lower accuracy (87.3 to 77.3) unless paired with a monitor.
agent_test: Maintain an explicit hypothesis list and choose tests that prune it; ablate the monitor.

claim: Working backwards (reverse thinking via distillation) improves small students (+13.53% average) but only a search snippet supports this.
agent_test: Check whether backward verification of an answer adds accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Escalating on answer disagreement beats fixed test-time strategies at the same sampling cap with thinking models: two agreeing samples stop, mild disagreement gets a vote, persistent disagreement gets a rewritten problem. Qwen3-8B across 7 math sets: base 61.3, majority vote 68.9, routed 75.8 at 6 samplings; the router used 40-70% of the cap. Counted in samplings, not tokens; false agreement is a stated failure case.
agent_test: Replicate on our own task mix with a token cap: 2 cheap samples, vote on mild disagreement, reformulate on persistent disagreement; compare to the best single strategy and to 6-sample majority.

claim: Learned per-item strategy routing gains little accuracy but cuts cost: Select-then-Solve router 53.1% vs best fixed paradigm 50.3% vs Direct 47.6%, recovering 26% of the oracle gap (oracle +17.1 over best single), at about 7.0k tokens per GPT-5 task vs 14.0k for always-ReAct. The oracle counts a single lucky run per paradigm, so the true gap is smaller.
agent_test: Estimate the oracle gap on our mix with repeated runs (3+ per strategy) so luck is separated from real complementarity; only build a router if the repeat-corrected gap is large.

claim: Asking the model to pick its own strategy is unreliable below the frontier: zero-shot self-routing helped only GPT-5 (67.1 vs Direct 60.3) while Qwen3-Max (42.4) and Qwen3-30B (27.5) fell below their Direct baselines, mostly over-picking tool paradigms.
schema_part: Strategy choice by measured signal, not self-report
agent_test: Compare self-chosen strategy vs disagreement-chosen vs fixed on our models; log how often the self-choice is the same strategy.

claim: Agents are slow to notice that the best option has silently changed, and an explicit rule (reuse the last success, switch after a failure) fixes this only for capable models: set-shifting accuracy gpt-5.5 0.14 to 0.86, deepseek-v4-pro 0.38 to 0.74, little or negative effect on mimo-v2.5 and gemini-3.5-flash-lite. Setting is tool choice, not problem-solving strategy.
agent_test: Add a success-changed check to the scaffold and measure on a task where the best strategy flips mid-stream; test on a weaker model too.

claim: Long-horizon simulation runs derail in ways that look like Dorner's stereotyped, unchecked action: meltdown loops after a mistaken belief about a delivery (Vending-Bench, all models, not tied to context fill) and idle-drift (Claude Haiku 4.5 averaged about 40 idle days of 90 while writing coherent plans, CoffeeBench). A strong model with no reasoning ran Tailorshop above typical human trajectories (end value about 305k vs 138k for unaided people), so failure is model- and horizon-dependent.
schema_part: Monitor (belief check, no-op counter, repeated-action detector)
agent_test: Run a Tailorshop-like or vending-like sim with a no-op counter and a belief-vs-observation check; count derailments with and without them.

claim: Problem solving before instruction beats instruction before problem solving for people with a moderate pooled effect (g 0.36, 95% CI 0.20-0.51; 53 studies, 166 comparisons; 0.37-0.58 with high-fidelity Productive Failure; 0.87 after bias correction), but young pupils and domain-general skills favour instruction first. No LLM test of an attempt-then-retrieve analogue was found.
schema_part: Order of attempt and method retrieval
agent_test: A/B at equal tokens: attempt first, then retrieve a method, vs retrieve first. Score on transfer items.

claim: Plain chain-of-thought prompts add little for reasoning models: GPQA Diamond o3-mini +2.9 points, o4-mini +3.1, Gemini Flash 2.5 -3.3, at 20-80% more time; with GPT-5 the best fixed paradigm is within 1.5 points of Direct on the full set. Decomposition, abstraction and analogy prompts have not been tested on reasoning models in the sources found.
agent_test: Ablate each prompted operator (decompose, abstract, analogy) on our thinking model at equal tokens before including it.

claim: A persistent per-task-type record of what worked helps agents when a small outside controller reads it (LIMBO bandit: equal or better accuracy at up to 83% lower cost, 53% on average; MemCon bandit: +2.6 to +4.2 points over G-Memory, 10.9-24.1% fewer tokens), but LLMs given raw history do not explore well in-context (only GPT-4 with CoT and externally summarised statistics worked). No test of the LLM reading its own strategy-success table was found.
agent_test: Keep a table of tries and successes per strategy and task type, show the summary (not the log) to the agent, compare to no table and to an outside bandit.

claim: Strategy as a callable operation beats strategy as a fixed script: on Smolbenchmark math, Llama3.3-70B scored 52.8 baseline, 66.0 with cognitive prompting (fixed order), 80.0 with the same four operations offered as tools; GPT-4.1 on AIME 2024 went 32.0, 42.0, 53.0 (o1-preview 44.6). Instruct models and 30 AIME items; no test on RL reasoning models.
schema_part: Unit of strategy = operator the agent invokes
agent_test: Compare fixed-order operator script vs operators offered on demand, same tokens.
